To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain density of δ‐receptor protein can be selectively reduced in rats by i.c.v. infusion of antisense oligodeoxynucelotides targeting the DOR mRNA sequence 280–300.

the density of rat brain δ‐receptor is decreased by i.c.v. injection of an antisense oligodeoxynucletide (aODN) targeting the DOR exon 2, and that the behavioural effects of the selective δ‐opioid antagonist SNC80 are abolished in rats with a δ‐receptor density reduced to 52% of that in controls.
the density of δ opioid receptors in rat forebrain is reduced significantly by aODN280‐299, but not by aODNs targeting exons 1, 2 or 3 of rat δ‐opoid receptor gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of aODN to decrease the density of δ opioid receptor in the CNS of rats, and the effects of the resulting δ‐knockout rats on opioid‐dependent behaviours.
the development of aODNs as potential drugs for treatment of pain.
the effects of selective knockdown of δ‐opioids in rat brain on locomotor behaviour and colonic propulsion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the density of δ opioid receptors in the CNS can be reduced by i.c.v. injection of an aODN to a specific sequence in exon 2 of the DOR gene, but this reduction does not alter the behavioural effects of a δ‐opioid selective agonist.
the DOR knockdown in rats is associated with decreased locomotion and colonic transit in the presence of a δ‐opioid ligand, but not with changes in nociception.

antisense oligonudeotides to the DOR mRNA sequence 280–399 significantly reduce brain δ‐opioids receptors, and that this effect is associated with a reduction of SNC80‐stimulated locomotor activity and colonic transit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the density of DOR protein can be reduced by aODN280‐299, but the behavioural and pharmacological responses to the δ‐opioid ligand SNC80 are only marginally affected by the reduced density of DOR.
the density of DOR in rat brain is regulated by a DOR‐specific aODN and that this regulation is functionally relevant.
the DOR‐knockdown in rat brain is associated with a significant reduction of locomotor activity in a novel environment and of SNC80‐stimulated motor behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the density of δ opioid receptors in rat brains can be reduced by antisense oligodeoxynuclotides.
the DOR is an important regulator of motor activity and colonic transit, and that the DOR can be targeted by antisense oligodeoxynucelotides.
the DOR is an important target for analgesic drug discovery.
